title: Publishing one story re-reads every published story and blocks for minutes (O(N) per publish, lease failures)
description:
As an editor publishing a story, I want `papyrus ops content publish` (the `publishItem` mutation) to come back within seconds and the page to follow reliably, so that I never retry a publish that already worked and never lose an hour to lease failures.

Measured 2026-11-08 on Machines on Machines (about 160 published stories, about 7,000 References): one projection took 69 to 190 s and grew with the number of published stories. The content-actions log shows `papyrus_request_over_budget ... Item.GetItem x100, PublishedItem.GetPublishedItem x98` and `papyrus_unbounded_list PublishedItemSummary / PublishedItem`; 69 of 180 invocations in three hours failed with `Projection lease ... waited 120s`.

Causes (profiled with the site's own web/ directory and a call-counting fake client):
1. `llms-full.txt` (and the item-pages follow-up) need every Story's body, read as two serial AppSync requests a Story: 2N+5 requests a publish (326 at N=160).
2. The item-pages follow-up re-reads the whole PublishedItem table with bodies on every publish (a whole-table read) and holds the lease while it renders every item page.
3. Every listing page whose inputs digest moved is PUT again, one at a time, even when its bytes are identical (153 of 206 writes per publish), and each is purged at the edge.
4. AppSync gives a Lambda resolver about 30 s, so a synchronous `publishItem` that projects always times out on a big site; a retry then waits 120 s for the lease and fails.

Not included here (follow-ups): the site-side `DEPENDS_ON` declaration that would stop every Videos/Findings page being re-rendered on a Story publish (a Machines on Machines change); making the console's Publish button asynchronous; chunking the deploy render so queued publishes run between chunks.

```gherkin
Feature: Publishing one story costs the same whatever the size of the site

  Scenario: A publish reads a fixed number of records, whatever the number of published stories
    Given a site with 300 published stories whose pages were projected
    When an editor publishes one more story
    Then the projection reads at most 3 records one by one and lists the published summaries at most twice
    And with 600 published stories the same publish reads the same number of records

  Scenario: Pages whose bytes did not change are neither written nor purged
    Given a projected site on a store that can tell what it holds
    When an editor publishes one more story
    Then only the pages whose bytes changed are written and purged

  Scenario: The CLI publish returns at once and the page follows
    Given a site whose page takes a minute to build
    When an editor publishes a story from the CLI
    Then the answer says the page is being built, with a job id, within seconds
    And asking for the job's status says when the page is live

  Scenario: Publishing the same story again while it is being built joins the build
    Given the page of a story is being built
    When the editor publishes the same story again
    Then no second build is started and the answer names the running job

  Scenario: A build that finds the site busy is queued, not failed
    Given another projection holds the site's lease
    When a story's build starts
    Then it waits a few seconds at most, leaves the story queued and the lease holder builds it before letting go
